paper.title_en: Probing scotogenic dark matter via soft displaced leptons and missing energy at the LHC
paper.abstract_en: The compressed-spectrum regime of the scotogenic model, where the inert charged state <math altimg="si31.svg"><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>η</mi><mo>˜</mo></mover><mo>±</mo></msup></math> and the dark matter candidate N1 are nearly mass-degenerate (ΔM ≲ 20 GeV), remains largely inaccessible to current ATLAS and CMS displaced-lepton searches, which impose lepton pT ≳ 20–30 GeV requirements (and historically up to 65 GeV) that the soft decay products cannot satisfy. We propose a dedicated signal region, SR-SDL, targeting the process <math altimg="si32.svg"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>→</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>η</mi><mo>˜</mo></mover><mo>±</mo></msup><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>η</mi><mo>˜</mo></mover><mn>0</mn></msup></mrow></math> at <math altimg="si33.svg"><mrow><msqrt><mi>s</mi></msqrt><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>13.6</mn><mspace width="0.16em"/><mtext>TeV</mtext></mrow></math>, which produces a single soft displaced lepton (pT > 5 GeV, |d0| ∈ [5, 300] mm) together with large missing transverse energy from the invisible <math altimg="si34.svg"><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>η</mi><mo>˜</mo></mover><mn>0</mn></msup><mo>→</mo><mi>ν</mi><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> decay and initial-state radiation recoil. The key discriminating variables are a large-radius tracking requirement on the lepton impact parameter, a b-jet veto to suppress heavy-flavour backgrounds, and a signal <math altimg="si35.svg"><msubsup><mi>E</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></mrow><mtext>miss</mtext></msubsup></math> threshold at the trigger efficiency plateau. Against an estimated SM background of <math altimg="si36.svg"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>66</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>24</mn></mrow></math> events at <math altimg="si1.svg"><mrow><mn>300</mn><mspace width="0.16em"/><msup><mrow><mtext>fb</mtext></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>, eight of nine benchmark points with <math altimg="si37.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>η</mi><mo>˜</mo></mover><mo>±</mo></msup></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>150</mn></mrow></math>–500 GeV and <math altimg="si38.svg"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mi>τ</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></math>–300 mm satisfy the 95% CL exclusion criterion <math altimg="si39.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mtext>sig</mtext></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">></mo><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mrow><mn mathvariant="normal">95</mn><mo>%</mo><mspace width="0.16em"/><mtext>CL</mtext></mrow><mtext>excl</mtext></msubsup><mo>≃</mo><mn>18</mn></mrow></math>, with the Yukawa coupling excluded in the range <math altimg="si40.svg"><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>≲</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>0.4</mn><mtext>--</mtext><mn>1.4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo linebreak="goodbreak">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> (depending on <math altimg="si2.svg"><msub><mi>m</mi><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>η</mi><mo>˜</mo></mover><mo>±</mo></msup></msub></math>, from 500 to 150 GeV), corresponding to proper decay lengths cτ ≳ 10 mm that place the <math altimg="si31.svg"><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>η</mi><mo>˜</mo></mover><mo>±</mo></msup></math> decay within the displaced-track acceptance window. The same Yukawa couplings that place the <math altimg="si31.svg"><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>η</mi><mo>˜</mo></mover><mo>±</mo></msup></math> decay length inside the ATLAS inner detector also reproduce the observed sub-eV neutrino masses via the scotogenic one-loop mechanism, making the SR-SDL search a direct probe of the radiative mass-generation scale.
